description:
A fixture-receipt test fails on a process-cwd race roughly a third of full-suite runs, so a gate verdict can depend on test scheduling rather than the tree.

## Background

`test_utils::tests::test_profiled_repository_fixture_receipt_binds_setup_and_consumer_to_shared_runtime_target` panics intermittently under `cargo test --workspace`:

    thread '...' panicked at crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs:1745:9:
    compile the consumer artifact: error: Unable to proceed. Could not locate working directory.: No such file or directory (os error 2)

The failure is a race against another test's `TempDir`: the panicking test's cargo invocation resolves its working directory while a concurrently finishing test tears its temporary directory down. Observed during the `5a3ecba0` wave on 2026-08-13: roughly one failure per three `cargo test --workspace` runs on a 24-core host. Reproduced on a stashed base commit (two failures in six runs), so it predates that wave's changes and is not theirs.

A test that fails on scheduling is the same defect class `0708d692` removed from the gate scripts: a verdict decided by the machine rather than the tree. The suite runs under nextest in gate runs (process-per-test), where the exposure may differ from `cargo test`'s in-process threading — whether the gate path is affected must be established, not assumed.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The fixture-receipt test passes deterministically under repeated whole-suite runs on a multi-core host, evidenced by a run count that previously reproduced the failure.
- [hard] REQ-02: The fix removes the test's dependence on another test's working directory rather than retrying over it or widening timeouts.
- [hard] REQ-03: Whether the nextest gate path was exposed is established and recorded with the fix.
title: A fixture-receipt test races another test's TempDir and flakes a third of suite runs
